_meta.purpose: Country norms for resumes and CVs. Read by the renderer (paper size, page target), the screening check (no US-only advice outside en-US) and the recruiter persona via references/locale-norms.md. These are conventions, not rules: the job posting's own instructions always win.

fields.name: Human-readable region name.
fields.paper: letter | a4. Paper size for the rendered resume.
fields.pages_student: Page target (maximum) for students and recent graduates. The renderer reports overflow above this.
fields.word: What English speakers in this market usually call the document: resume | CV.
fields.local_word: The usual local-language term, for non-English documents.
fields.photo: omit | optional | customary. omit = not expected, remove it; optional = acceptable either way, never a red flag, never add one just for this; customary = commonly included locally, but never required and leaving it out is fine.
fields.dob: omit | optional | customary. Same meaning as photo, for date of birth or age.
fields.personal_details: omit | optional | customary. Marital status, nationality, place of birth. Never infer or comment on protected traits either way.
fields.notes: Short, plain-language guidance for the recruiter persona and the report.
fields.confidence: high | medium | low: how well the sources below agree.
fields.uncertain: Fields where sources disagree or no authoritative source was found.

en-US.name: United States
en-US.gpa_note: 4.0 scale. List it if it is 3.0 or higher or the posting asks for it.
notes: One page is the norm for students and recent graduates; two pages are fine once you have several years of relevant experience.
Leave out a photo, date of birth, age and marital status. US employers do not expect them.
3.0 is the most common GPA cutoff among employers that screen by GPA, and fewer employers screen by GPA than a few years ago. Never add a GPA the candidate did not give.
City and state are enough for location; a full street address is not needed.

en-CA.name: Canada
en-CA.gpa_note: Scales differ by province and school (4.0, 4.3, 9-point, percentages). Include it only if strong or requested, with the scale.
notes: One page is the usual target for students; two pages is the upper limit the Government of Canada Job Bank recommends.
Leave out a photo, age, marital status, religion and other personal details. Never include a Social Insurance Number.
In Quebec, a French-language resume may be expected; follow the posting.

en-GB.name: United Kingdom
en-GB.gpa_note: Degree classification: First, 2:1 (upper second), 2:2 (lower second), Third. Current students often give a predicted or expected classification. A-level grades are common for graduates.
notes: No longer than two sides of A4; a shorter CV is fine for part-time student jobs, and very senior roles may run to three.
No photo unless the role is acting or modelling, and no date of birth.
Give the degree classification (or expected classification), not a GPA. Changing a classification, for example 2:2 to 2:1, counts as degree fraud.
Call the document a CV.

en-IE.name: Ireland
en-IE.gpa_note: Honours degree classes: First Class Honours, Second Class Honours Grade 1 (2.1), Grade 2 (2.2), Third, Pass. Leaving Certificate points or grades are sometimes listed by recent school leavers.
notes: Two pages is the usual length.
A photo is not the convention in Ireland; leave out date of birth and marital status unless an application explicitly asks.
Give the degree classification (or expected classification), not a GPA.

en-AU.name: Australia
en-AU.gpa_note: Many universities report GPA on a 7-point scale or a weighted average mark (WAM, a percentage); honours degrees carry a class (First Class, 2A, 2B, Third). Include with the scale if strong or requested.
notes: Two pages is the usual target for graduates; experienced candidates often run to three. Published guidance ranges from one to four pages, so follow the posting.
Leave out a photo, date of birth, marital status, religion and nationality.
Referees (usually two) are common; 'referees available on request' is also acceptable. Never list a referee's details without asking them.
Australian Public Service roles often ask you to address selection criteria in a separate document.

en-NZ.name: New Zealand
en-NZ.gpa_note: Universities report letter grades, and some calculate a GPA (scales differ by university). Include with the scale if strong or requested.
notes: New Zealand CVs are typically two to three pages; two is enough for most graduates.
Leave out a photo, date of birth and marital status.
Referees are commonly listed near the end, with their permission.

en-IN.name: India
en-IN.local_word: resume (CV and biodata are also used)
en-IN.gpa_note: CGPA on a 10-point scale or a percentage, for each degree (and often class 10 and 12 results for freshers). Campus recruiters frequently set a cutoff.
notes: One page is common for freshers in private-sector and campus hiring; two pages with experience.

Practice is mixed: older formats include a photo, date of birth and other personal details, while many private-sector and multinational employers no longer expect them. Do not treat either choice as a red flag.
Government and public-sector applications may require a specific biodata format; follow the notification.
List CGPA or percentage with its scale.

de-DE.name: Germany
de-DE.gpa_note: German scale from 1.0 (best) to 5.0, with 4.0 the usual pass mark. Give the final or current grade (Abschlussnote) in the German system if you include it.
notes: A tabular, reverse-chronological Lebenslauf of one to two pages is usual; some experienced candidates use three.
A professional photo is still common but has not been required since the General Equal Treatment Act (AGG, 2006); leaving it out is fine and is never a red flag.
Date of birth and nationality often appear under personal details; they are optional.
Applications often include certificates and references (Zeugnisse) as attachments.

de-AT.name: Austria
de-AT.gpa_note: Austrian scale from 1 (Sehr gut, best) to 5 (Nicht genügend, fail).
notes: A photo is common, but the Austrian government's guidance says photo, date of birth, place of birth and citizenship are all voluntary.
A tabular, reverse-chronological Lebenslauf of up to two pages is usual.
Some guidance suggests signing a printed CV; for digital applications this is optional.

de-CH.name: Switzerland
de-CH.gpa_note: Swiss scale from 1 to 6, where 6 is best and 4 is a pass. Universities may also report ECTS grades.
notes: A professional photo, date of birth, nationality and sometimes marital status are usual on a Swiss CV, but none is mandatory.
Applications are often sent as a full dossier: CV, cover letter, diplomas and employment certificates (Arbeitszeugnisse).
Write in the language of the posting (German, French or Italian, or English for international employers).

fr-FR.name: France
fr-FR.gpa_note: Grades out of 20, often with an honours mention (assez bien, bien, très bien). Name the diploma (Licence, Master, BTS, DUT/BUT) and the school.
notes: One page is widely advised for students and recent graduates; two pages with experience.
A photo is optional and not required unless requested; if included it should be professional.
Age or date of birth sometimes appears on French CVs; it is optional.
Recent graduates often put education (Formation) first.

es-ES.name: Spain
es-ES.gpa_note: Spanish scale from 0 to 10, with 5 a pass; matrícula de honor is the top distinction. Give the average (nota media) with its scale if you include it.
notes: One to two pages is usual.

Sources disagree: some describe a photo and date of birth as common on Spanish CVs, while a university careers office advises leaving them out unless the employer asks. Treat both as optional and never as a red flag.
Write in Spanish unless the posting is in English.

default.name: Other or unknown locale
default.gpa_note: Grading scales differ by country; include grades with their scale if strong or requested.
notes: Customs differ by country, so follow the job posting's instructions first.

A photo or date of birth is never a reason to reject, because customs differ by country. When building a new resume for an unknown market leave them out, but do not tell the candidate an existing one is a mistake.
A4 is the international default paper size; the United States and Canada use Letter.
When the locale is unclear, confirm it with the candidate in one line before the review.

nace_gpa_2022.title: NACE: Use of GPA as a candidate selection tool falls (Job Outlook 2022)
nace_gpa_2022.supports: 3.0 is the most common cutoff among employers that screen by GPA; the share of employers screening by GPA has fallen (46.3% in the fall 2022 survey).
nace_gpa_2022.seen_via: search summary and the panel research report; the page itself was not fetched in this build

us_otterbein.title: Otterbein University career center: Resume Guidelines
us_otterbein.supports: Undergraduates should aim for a one-page resume.

us_wcupa.title: West Chester University: Resumes and Cover Letters
us_wcupa.supports: One page of content recommended for most undergraduates.

us_psu_checklist.title: Penn State College of IST: Resume checklist
us_psu_checklist.supports: No photos; city and state only for location.

ca_job_bank.title: Government of Canada Job Bank: How to write a good resume
ca_job_bank.supports: Limit the resume to two pages; omit age, weight, height, marital status, religious preference and political views; do not include a picture; never include your Social Insurance Number.

uk_prospects.title: Prospects (Jisc): How to write a CV
uk_prospects.supports: CVs no longer than two A4 pages (three possible for senior roles); no photo unless acting or modelling; date of birth is irrelevant; include qualification grades; altering a degree grade is degree fraud.

ie_dcu.title: Dublin City University careers: How do I build a strong CV?
ie_dcu.supports: CV should be two pages; a photograph is not the convention for Ireland, the UK and the USA.

au_uq.title: University of Queensland Employability: Resume fact sheet
au_uq.supports: Professional resumes in Australia are generally two to four pages.
au_uq.seen_via: search summary (the PDF could not be read in this build)

au_veterans.title: Australian Government Veterans' Employment: Writing a resume
au_veterans.supports: Describes a resume as a short (one to two page) document.

au_asic.title: ASIC careers: Resume tips
au_asic.supports: A resume should be no more than four pages, depending on experience.

nz_knowyourcv.title: Careers New Zealand (careers.govt.nz): Tips for creating a NZ-style CV
nz_knowyourcv.supports: New Zealand CVs are typically about two to three pages.
nz_knowyourcv.seen_via: search summary (the page failed to load directly)

nz_otago.title: University of Otago careers: CV guide
nz_otago.supports: Two pages is enough for most New Zealand graduate CVs.

in_guides.title: Indian resume guides (commercial; no official source found)
in_guides.supports: Guides conflict: some keep date of birth, marital status and a declaration in a personal-details block, others advise private-sector freshers to leave out photo, date of birth and personal details; CGPA or percentage is listed per degree.
in_guides.seen_via: search summary; treat as low confidence

de_bremen.title: University of Bremen Career Center: Application documents (applying in Germany)
de_bremen.supports: German CVs are one to two pages; a photo is no longer required under the General Equal Treatment Act (AGG); birthdate is listed under personal details; GPA is optional and should use the German grading system.

de_magdeburg.title: Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg: English CV (Lebenslauf) template
de_magdeburg.supports: Maximum two pages for young professionals and three for experienced professionals; photo not compulsory but appreciated.

at_oesterreich_gv.title: oesterreich.gv.at (Austrian government portal): Bewerbungstipps
at_oesterreich_gv.supports: Citizenship, date of birth and place of birth may be given voluntarily; a photo is likewise voluntary; a printed CV is usually signed.

ch_zhaw.title: ZHAW School of Management and Law career services: CV / Lebenslauf
ch_zhaw.supports: A photo is not mandatory in Switzerland, but it is common practice.

ch_swissinfo.title: swissinfo.ch: From CV to interview, how to apply for a job
ch_swissinfo.supports: Personal information such as a photo, date of birth and marital status is quite usual on a Swiss CV.

fr_apecita.title: Apecita (APEC network for agri-food careers): CV advice card
fr_apecita.supports: A photo on a French CV is optional; if used, it should be recent and professional.

es_ucm.title: Universidad Complutense de Madrid careers office: El currículum vitae (2012)
es_ucm.supports: Advises leaving out photo and birth date unless the employer asks (document dates from 2012).

es_guides.title: Commercial Spanish CV guides
es_guides.supports: Describes a photo as customary but declining (especially in tech), date of birth as a common personal field, and one to two pages as usual.
es_guides.seen_via: search summary; treat as low confidence

_unverified: Grade scales (Swiss 1-6, Austrian 1-5, German 1.0-5.0, French marks out of 20, Spanish 0-10, Indian 10-point CGPA, Australian 7-point GPA and WAM, Irish and UK classifications) are stated from general knowledge and were not each checked against an official source in this build.
No official source was found for India, France or Spain on photos and dates of birth; their values are deliberately 'optional' with low confidence.
Several sources were read only through search-result summaries, as marked in seen_via; re-check them before quoting exact wording.
